title: IDisposable and using
sub: Release a resource now, not someday
cards/0/title: Resources the GC doesn't know about
cards/0/body:
A file, a network connection, a database connection: these are OS resources. The GC only sees memory and has no idea an object is holding a file open.

If you wait for the GC, the file may stay open for who knows how long.
cards/1/task: Open the file, then "forget" it (= null) and try to open it again. Get the second open to succeed without Dispose.
cards/2/body:
Classes that hold such resources implement IDisposable: the Dispose() method closes the resource right away.

using calls Dispose() automatically, even if an exception was thrown inside.
cards/3/task: Now open the file twice the right way: with Dispose() or using.
cards/4/q: An exception was thrown inside a using block. What happens to the resource?
cards/4/explain: using expands into try/finally, and finally runs no matter what.
cards/5/q: using is syntactic sugar. What does it expand into?
cards/5/explain: try/finally guarantees Dispose() on both a normal exit and an exception.
cards/6/title: Your own class with a resource
cards/6/body: If a class owns an IDisposable field, it must implement IDisposable too and release the field in its own Dispose(). No finalizer needed.
cards/6/deep: The full Dispose(bool disposing) pattern with GC.SuppressFinalize(this) is for unsealed classes that may have subclasses, and for classes that hold an unmanaged resource directly. For the latter there's SafeHandle, the next lesson.
cards/7/q: A class stores a FileStream in a field. What's the right move?
cards/7/options/0: Implement IDisposable and call _file.Dispose() in Dispose()
cards/7/options/1: Write a finalizer that closes the file
cards/7/options/2: Nothing: the GC will close it
cards/7/explain: The owner of a resource passes the responsibility up: its callers will wrap it in using too.
cards/8/q: What is true? Select all that apply.
cards/8/options/0: Dispose() releases the resource right away, without waiting for the GC
cards/8/options/1: After Dispose() the object may still live in memory
cards/8/options/2: using calls Dispose() even on an exception
cards/8/explain: Dispose closes the OS resource. The object's own memory is still freed by the GC once the object becomes unreachable.
